- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict early in the horizon (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows low volatility, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture mean reversion.
- If true outcome deviates >2% from forecast in first 3 days, model is likely biased; apply correction based on sentiment direction: bullish → reduce, bearish → increase.
